summary: Critiqued all 7 scored counter-claim records against the original brief. 3 original claims did not survive as stated and were falsified/reversed by stronger evidence: pie-vs-bar chart superiority (peer-reviewed 2025 study contradicts 'consistently outperform'), skeleton screens 'preferred over spinners' (a controlled study found the opposite on every metric), and truncated Y-axes as a blanket anti-pattern (two independent data-viz authorities say the rule is bar-chart-specific, not chart-type-agnostic). 2 original claims held with an added caveat rather than being contradicted: Material Design's 15.8:1 contrast figure (descriptive claim unchallenged; halation/astigmatism caveat added) and content-form-fit distinctiveness (NN/g familiarity research adds an interaction-convention caveat but doesn't oppose the core claim). 2 sub-claims remain genuinely unresolved (Studio Meyer's 15-30% FPS figure; bento grids at high information density) with no credible evidence on either side, consistent with the brief's own flagged risks. No claim traced to a source that doesn't actually support it, and the counter-evidence side engaged substantively with every target claim, so no bounce is warranted.
